proof.surface: Two envoy-dispatch processes on one database. A reaches the listener through the 2 s latency proxy. B reaches it through slowsend.py, which forwards every request at once and holds only the answer to POST /v1/messages/send for 7 s, so B's send lands and B's 5 s window runs out. ses-y advertises steer and aside.
proof.command: timedretry.sh head-none none; timedretry.sh head-route route (6 person comments on LGA-7 mention ses-y on A, so c6's attempt 1 waits queued in A's lane; c6 is then retried in aside through B)
proof.observed: The Retry answers 201 with attempt 2 failed, 'the message may already have been delivered'; the proxy log shows the listener answered that send 200. A's lane then sends attempt 1, which the listener answers duplicate=true. Attempt 1 settles sent, nothing stays pending, there is no fallback row, and ses-y stores c1-c6 once each. The routed run gives the same result.
proof.negativeControl: timedretry.sh r15-none none on round 15's build edaaae7e: attempt 1 is sent with duplicate=false, and ses-y stores c6 twice.
